query: What does the conversation reveal about how thoroughly each member of the book club actually reads the books?
gold: The group's reading rigour varies considerably. Tomasz is the most thorough reader — he page-references his observations ('on page 218...', 'from page 147 onwards') and reads including the author's note. Blessing reads as a professional writer — close attention to craft, structure, and what's unsaid. Harriet reads fully but with a specific interpretive agenda she pursues rather than opens. Graham reads carefully but may focus on the opening chapters: Tomasz asked him whether he'd read the second chapter after he made a claim that the second chapter resolves. Nadia demonstrably does not read the full book: she pivots to 'what did everyone make of the ending?' without offering her own view, borrows Blessing's reading and claims she 'was going to say the same thing', and asks about 'the middle section' in terms vague enough to invite others to specify which section.
context:
[1] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2025-08-25T19:54:00) can we not get competitive about who read what 😂 the point is we all engage with it differently and that's beautiful right? 📚
[2] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t0 @2025-08-04T11:41:00) I thought the ending undermined everything the first two-thirds had built. On page 342 the narrator explicitly says she won't forgive him, then she does. It felt like a different book.
[3] (about=Harriet, episodic, t0 @2025-08-04T11:48:00) I think we can all agree the ending is the point. The forgiveness is earned, you just have to read the whole arc rather than taking the page 342 quote out of context.
[4] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t6 @2025-08-25T19:48:00) Did you read the second chapter, Graham? The ambiguity you mention in the first chapter resolves by page 28.
[5] (about=Graham, episodic, t6 @2025-08-25T19:58:00) For the record I did read the second chapter, Tomasz.
[6] (about=Graham, episodic, t2 @2025-08-11T17:04:00) Sally Rooney sounds good to me. I'll read it properly this time.
[7] (about=Nadia, episodic, t4 @2025-08-18T11:05:00) I just liked the scene by the kitchen window 😭 everyone is so much smarter than me
[8] (about=Nadia, episodic, t4 @2025-08-18T10:41:00) Blessing I love how you read things 🥹 what did everyone make of the middle section? I found it so interesting
[9] (about=Blessing, episodic, t4 @2025-08-18T10:22:00) I think the book is doing something different from that reading, Harriet. The class stuff is surface. What Rooney is actually doing is showing how intimacy becomes a proxy for power, and the power isn't class-based, it's gendered. Two different books depending on which character you center.
[10] (about=Blessing, episodic, t4 @2025-08-18T10:34:00) I do have the context, I wrote about it for the TLS. The class reading is valid but it's not the only one. Multiple readings can be right simultaneously.
[11] (about=Blessing, episodic, t6 @2025-08-25T19:35:00) Graham your reading wasn't dismissed, we just added to it. That's the whole point of a discussion. Multiple readings can live together.
[12] (about=Harriet, episodic, t7 @2025-09-01T21:02:00) I've been thinking about last month. I think my book club is at its best when we have genuine disagreement. I'll grant Blessing that. Even if I still think the class reading is the correct one.
[13] (about=Tomasz, episodic, t6 @2025-08-25T20:16:00) Provided the book is chosen by then.
agent_answer: Tomasz, Harriet, and Blessing appear to read the books thoroughly — Tomasz cites specific pages and challenges others, Harriet insists on reading the whole arc, and Blessing offers nuanced contextual analyses and professional expertise. Graham seems less thorough, since Tomasz questions whether he read the second chapter and Graham admits he will "read it properly this time," implying past lapses. Nadia seems to read but less deeply or analytically, as she self-deprecates and mainly reacts to scenes or asks questions rather than offering detailed interpretations.
